observable_outcome: Provider compatibility is defined as two named relations and reported as two declared intervals with an explicit unknown: which Provider CLI versions each adapter supports, and which Loop versions carry that adapter contract. No self-claim is authority for either. An incompatible Provider opens the contract-incompatible circuit, which is never probe-eligible and closes only on an explicitly observed version change, and a version measured outside the declared interval is refused before a Request exists rather than discovered by spending an invocation. When work must move, a single declared decision function is the only thing that may produce a handoff target: it triggers on the source being not-sendable -- the circuit not sending, or the usage window exhausted, or the pool slot needing an owner's action -- filters candidates by the owner's standing authorization, by declared compatibility and by the attempt history for that Increment, and returns either a handoff target or one closed waiting reason per table cell. The owner sees, per Provider, the two intervals, the compatibility state, the exhaustion state, and either the proposed handoff target or why the Loop is waiting. The handoff loses nothing: the carried content digest is preserved across all six ordered Provider pairs and any loss is a refusal.
acceptance_criteria: A1. Scope boundary and the fixture-versus-live split, written before any code. The evidence opens with a table stating, one row each: what this task decides (the two compatibility relations and their authorities), what it wires (the single-producer handoff decision), what it reports (the two declared intervals, the compatibility state, the exhaustion state and the disposition), what it deliberately does not do (no observed CLI version reaches the control plane, no request DTO is widened, internal/runner is not edited, no store port is added, no d12 opening-table row changes and no breaker, pool or window behaviour changes), and what only V2-028 can establish. The V2-028 row must list, individually: that a declared interval is true of a real CLI; that a real exhaustion or a real contract break produces the class the table assumes; that a real handoff preserves the Increment, Artifact and Evidence through a real journal, lease and Evidence record; and that the waiting reason an owner sees in a Preview journey is the one the capability's journey requires. Nothing in the evidence may claim any release gate, any M6 completion condition, or that production hands off today.

A2. Baseline, measured before changing anything, with every line number re-measured rather than copied. Record top-level test names and counts and that all pass for internal/provider (57 at the starting commit), internal/application (107), internal/api (36), internal/store/memory (8), internal/contracts (30) and internal/release (47). These counts and every line number in this Work Order were read at commit 2d1a514 and are expected to be stale: run devbox run --pure -- go test -list '.*' on each package, re-grep every cited line, use the measured value, and report every disagreement. Record as measured facts: nothing outside internal/provider constructs a Pool, Breaker or UsageWindow or calls ApplyObservation, PrepareHandoff, ChainHandoff or RequestFromHandoff, established by a search over every *.go file in the module outside that package, with the argv recorded; NewBreaker creates every circuit closed regardless of the slot and ActionMoveSlotWithoutOpening touches only the pool, so an unauthenticated slot reports a sending circuit; RequestFromHandoff consults only the breaker; ProviderObservationInput's field list is pinned to exactly three names by an existing test in internal/application; internal/provider/adapters_test.go's nine-case matrix already asserts cli-version-incompatible produces contract-incompatible for all three adapters; the fixture manifest declares cli_version_declared per entry with the measured values 0.149.1 for codex, 2.1.241 for claude and 1.18.22 for opencode; ci/components.json declares application's dependencies as domain, infra and release, and provider as a leaf with none. Every pre-existing test must still pass at the end under its existing name with its existing assertions unchanged, and before/after top-level counts per touched package must be reported.

A3. The two relations are declared, closed and total. In internal/provider declare, per adapter, the supported Provider CLI version interval, and, per contract version, the supported Loop version interval. Assert: each interval is half-open and non-empty; the declared version of each adapter's own fixture entries lies inside that adapter's interval, read from internal/provider/testdata/manifest.json rather than from a second copy; the compatibility function is total over a table that includes a version below the interval, at the lower bound, inside, at the upper bound, above the interval, an empty version, and a version that does not match the declared semver shape -- with the verdict for each, and unknown for the empty and malformed cases; and no verdict enum spells compatible without unknown being a sibling member of the same closed set, asserted by parsing the declaration rather than by reading it.

A4. Authority, asserted rather than asserted-in-prose. Assert by AST scan that the compatibility declaration is read from source and never from a Provider response envelope: no code path in internal/provider assigns a supported interval from parsed fixture bytes, and the fixture's own cli_version_declared field is never used as the authority for the interval. Assert that no request-admission path reads any type this task declares, by an AST scan over internal/api/auth.go and internal/application's caller path modelled on the equivalent V2-069 scan, and by a behavioural test in which a request whose Provider is declared incompatible still succeeds unchanged at every route it succeeded at before. Record the four-row authority table from dp-v2-074 d2 verbatim in the evidence and in the documentation, including the row that says only V2-028 can establish that a declared interval is true.

A5. Incompatibility opens the existing circuit and nothing new. Assert, using the three cli-version-incompatible fixtures through ParseOrClassify for all three adapters: the class is contract-incompatible; the opening table's action for it is open-immediately; the resulting circuit reports not-sending with that class in its stated reason and the observation scope attached; Probe refuses with ErrProbeNotEligible however much time passes; and ObserveDeclaredCLIVersion closes it only for a version different from the one recorded at the open, and not for the same version and not for an empty one. Do not edit internal/provider/breaker.go, internal/provider/breaker_test.go or the d12 opening table, and do not add a FailureClass. If any of these behaviours is not already true, stop and escalate rather than changing the breaker.

A6. The pre-invocation refusal, fail-closed on measured and fail-open on unknown. provider.Request gains exactly one optional field, CLIVersionDeclared, and the shared build helper refuses with ErrInvalidRequest when it is non-empty and measured outside the adapter's declared interval. Assert: refusal for all three adapters with a below-interval and an above-interval version, with no Invocation returned; no refusal when the field is empty; no refusal for a version inside the interval; that Request.Validate's existing verdicts are unchanged for every existing case; and that adding the field changes no existing assertion about Request or Invocation. Record in the evidence, in these words, that no production caller supplies the field, that the refusal is therefore exercised by tests and not by production, and who owns arming it. Do not edit internal/runner to supply it.

A7. The Sendable predicate and the trigger, declared as one total table. Declare Sendable over the three inputs -- circuit state in {sending, not-sending, probing}, window state in {within-window, exhausted, unknown}, slot state in the pool's six declared states -- and assert the table is total over the full cross product with no default branch, by enumerating the product in the test rather than sampling it. Assert specifically, each as its own named case: probing holds rather than hands off; window unknown does not trigger; window exhausted does trigger; slot in-use holds rather than hands off; slot unauthenticated, quarantined and stopped-for-inspection each make the source not-sendable; and cancelled and invalid-input observations move nothing, driven through ApplyObservation so the assertion is about the real path. Assert that no FailureClass is synthesized for a window exhaustion: the diff contains no assignment of a FailureClass derived from a window state, checked by AST scan, and ApplyObservation's behaviour is byte-identical for every input it accepted before.

A8. The disposition function and its target filters. DecideHandoff returns a closed disposition in {none, handoff-proposed, waiting} with a target or a waiting reason, and is the only function in the package that may produce a handoff target. Assert: the candidate order is deterministic and is the declared PoolNames order, verified by driving the same state twice and comparing byte-identical results; a candidate the owner's standing authorization does not cover is refused, and so is one whose slot needs an owner's action -- this is non_goal 2 and must be asserted for both shapes; a candidate whose declared version is measured incompatible is refused, while one whose compatibility is unknown is NOT refused, with both cases run; a candidate already in the attempt history for this Increment is refused; and the chain bound is respected. Assert by AST scan that RequestFromHandoff is referenced from exactly one non-test location in the module and that DecideHandoff is the only producer of the target it receives; verify the scanner first against a known-positive and a known-negative. Do not change RequestFromHandoff's signature or its existing verdicts, and do not edit its existing test cases.

A9. The measured defect from dp-v2-074 d7 is demonstrated and closed at the decision, and its residual is recorded. Assert as a positive control, before the fix, that a Provider whose slot is unauthenticated reports a sending circuit and is accepted by RequestFromHandoff -- run it, record the result, and keep it as a test that documents why the decision consults the slot. Then assert DecideHandoff refuses that Provider as a target. Record in the evidence that RequestFromHandoff remains callable with a hand-picked target and would still accept such a target, that the AST single-caller guard is what makes that unreachable in this tree, that a guard is weaker than a signature, and that widening the signature was rejected only because it would stop existing tests compiling under their own names. Name the owner of closing the residual.

A10. The waiting reason vocabulary, derived not invented. Derive the members mechanically as exactly one reason per cell of the decision table whose disposition is waiting, and assert both directions of totality: a waiting cell with no reason fails, and a declared reason no cell can produce fails. Assert that the vocabulary shares no member with the queue waiting reason V2-068 introduces, that neither vocabulary is empty, and record the two member lists side by side in the documentation so an owner cannot read one as the other. If V2-068 has not landed, stop and escalate rather than guessing its vocabulary: this task's chain position is immediately after it for exactly this reason.

A11. The handoff loses nothing, at the strength a fixture can prove. Assert that for all six ordered pairs of the three Provider names, a disposition of handoff-proposed followed by the existing conversion yields a Request whose packet carries a content digest identical to the source's, computed by the existing HandoffContentDigest and not by a second copy of it; and that dropping or mutating any one of IncrementID, Constraints, Decisions, Artifacts, Verification and Unresolved produces a refusal rather than a repair. Record explicitly that this is fixture-level preservation only, that V2-027 already established the same property for the conversion and attributed preservation through a real journal, lease, Increment and Evidence record to V2-028, and that this task adds only the property that the decision in front of the conversion loses nothing either.

A12. The application-side derivation and the by-value pinning. Declare the same decision table in internal/application over the same shared normalised input tuple, mapping health, blocked_reason, runaway state, concurrency exhaustion, standing authorization and the assignment ring onto that tuple. Assert: each mapping is total over its own closed enums, so a new enum member on either side fails a test on that side; the two tables agree cell by cell, compared by value in a pinning test; and internal/application imports neither internal/provider nor internal/runner, re-running the existing import scan under its own name. Write no module-path string literal into any file: internal/ci's manifest check reads such a literal as an undeclared edge and turns make check red, so build any needed path by concatenating a prefix with a suffix.

A13. The read surface. ProviderEntryView gains a compatibility block (the declared Provider CLI version interval, the declared Loop version interval, the observed Loop version or its absence, and two verdicts each in a closed set whose members include unknown) and a handoff block (disposition, target, waiting reason). Add both to the ProviderRegistryEntry schema in contracts/openapi/openapi-v1.yaml, which sets additionalProperties:false so every field is forced to be declared, and keep the entry's fixed order and the response's exactly-three-entries bound. Assert: the response carries no field this Work Order did not name; GET /v1/providers keeps its existing status codes, owner-only role gating and byte-identical output for repeated calls against the same stored state; the observed Loop version is absent rather than synthesized when no release observer is configured, and the loop verdict is then unknown; no threshold number and no ceiling value appears anywhere in either block; and both existing vocabulary scans pass unchanged -- V2-067's ban over the emitted read-model JSON keys and internal/provider's ban over declared identifiers. Assert the measured read count for one GET /v1/providers is unchanged from the baseline and still independent of the Requirement count.

A14. No new port and no store change. Assert that neither internal/store/memory nor internal/store/firestore is edited and that UnitOfWork gains no method, by git diff. The disposition must be derivable from what one bounded keyed read per Provider already returns, including the assignment ring's IncrementID. If a stored fact turns out to be missing, stop and escalate: adding a port obliges both adapters and puts this task in two more chain file groups, and the Firestore read-cost property is gated by docs/architecture/validation.md section 5.

A15. Owner console. Append one self-contained block to internal/web/owner.html and one to internal/web/owner.js, each introduced by a comment naming V2-074, at the end of the file, changing no existing byte. The blocks must render, per Provider: the two declared intervals, the compatibility state with unknown shown as unknown and never as compatible or blank, the exhaustion state, and either the proposed handoff target or the waiting reason in plain words. Add no external asset, script or font. Assert the rendered markup contains no credential-shaped and no email-shaped value, and no threshold number.

A16. Documentation. docs/operations/provider-registry.md gains sections stating: the two relations and why compatibility is not defined Provider-CLI-to-Loop directly; the four-row authority table; that no observed CLI version reaches the control plane and why the DTO was not widened; the Sendable table and the trigger judgement with the reason each rejected alternative was rejected, quoting the opening-table rows it would contradict; the disposition table with its waiting reasons and the disjointness from V2-068's queue vocabulary; the fixture-versus-V2-028 split; and the two residuals with their owners. Correct the two sentences in that document that currently say the registry cannot decide a handoff and introduces no version-compatibility check, keeping the historical statement visible rather than deleting it. docs/operations/provider-adapters.md gains the declared intervals beside the measured argv surfaces. Do not edit docs/operations/provider-live-claude.md, docs/operations/self-update.md, docs/architecture/**, docs/preview/** or docs/stable/**.

A17. The capability declaration is not weakened, and the derivation is written out. Quote cap-provider-operation's observable_result verbatim in the evidence and map each clause to the field or table that satisfies it: 接続済みか to authorized and verified_by_loop_invocation; 対応version to the declared Provider CLI version interval; 認証の健全性 to health and blocked_reason; 同時実行上限 to the concurrency block; 利用上限・枯渇状態 to the exhaustion state; 対応Loop Version to the declared Loop version interval; 現在の割当先Requirement to the assignments; and handoff-or-waiting to the disposition block. For every clause this task does not fully satisfy, state which part is missing and who owns it. Do not edit contracts/release-contract/** and do not narrow, reword or reinterpret any declared clause to make it satisfiable.

A18. Determinism. No fixed sleep, no wall-clock timer and no goroutine in any new test; every instant comes from an injected clock and every wait, if any is needed at all, is a bounded deadline poll. Every table test enumerates its cross product rather than sampling it. Run devbox run --pure -- go test -count=1 ./internal/provider ./internal/application ./internal/api three times in sequence and record that the verdict line and the output are identical each time, and run it once with -race. Judge every run by the verdict line, not by the shell exit status. Do not start a Provider CLI: --help and --version are the only Provider CLI reads permitted, and no invocation of any kind may be made by this task.

A19. Measured notes for V2-045, recorded and not acted on. Record which import edges this task creates -- by design, none: internal/provider stays a leaf, internal/application imports neither provider nor runner and gains no new dependency beyond the release dependency it already declares, and internal/api and internal/web are unchanged in their dependencies. Record that the task moves the provider, application, api, web, contracts and docs component keys, and that editing contracts/openapi/openapi-v1.yaml moves the contracts key, a declared contract dependency of the api and control-plane components. Only the provider, application and api evidence records are issued here; name V2-045 as the owner of the remaining key movement under gate rule G6. Because this design creates no edge, a red manifest or dependency-coverage check in make check means the design was departed from: stop and escalate to the tech_lead and do not edit ci/components.json, Makefile, go.mod, go.sum or devbox.*.

A20. Escalations, recorded not closed. Record, each with a named owner: that two of the three Provider CLIs have no authenticated session on this machine and no agent can create one, so a real handoff between two real Providers is owner-blocked rather than deferred; that the pre-invocation refusal is unarmed in production; that the RequestFromHandoff residual stands; and that the observed-CLI verdict is unknown until a Runner client exists. Do not weaken, relax or reword any assertion to make any of these disappear.

A21. Evidence. Create .agents/v2/evidence/V2-074-provider.json (id ev-v2-074-provider, component provider), .agents/v2/evidence/V2-074-application.json (id ev-v2-074-application, component application) and .agents/v2/evidence/V2-074-api.json (id ev-v2-074-api, component api), each with task_id V2-074 and correlation_id v2-074-version-and-handoff, recording for every check the argv actually executed, the working directory, the timeout and a summary stating the measured result, with every acceptance item traceable to a named check. The provider record must carry the full Sendable cross-product table and the full disposition table, cell by cell, with the verdict for each. Record the execution environment identifier (uname -srm, go version as resolved inside devbox run --pure, devbox environment). A skipped test is recorded with status skipped and never counted as a pass (gate rule G7). Register the records with exactly three appended entries in .agents/v2/evidence/index.json whose evidence_hash is the sha256 of each artifact's final committed bytes; touch no other task's entry. devbox run --pure -- go test -count=1 ./internal/contracts must be green with the records in place. Any digest written in prose must be 64 or 40 hex characters followed by at most one punctuation character.

A22. Component evidence keys and their count, measured not predicted. The evidence_key recorded in each artifact is that component's key read with devbox run --pure -- make evidence-keys on the final tree where make check is green, with every touched file already git-added: a new file not yet in the index is invisible to the git ls-files based input set the key derives from. The number of keys that move is the transitive closure of the declared dependencies and has exceeded prediction in each of the last four tasks (predicted 7 measured 13; predicted 8 measured 14). Read the closure on the final green tree, issue the records with the values that tree reports, and report any difference from what this Work Order implies.

A23. Secret scan and final check. Run devbox run --pure -- gitleaks dir .agents --config .gitleaks.toml before every commit that touches .agents/**, never gitleaks dir . for that scan, and record the verdict. devbox run --pure -- make check must be green, and it is re-run after the evidence commit so the secret scan reads committed history rather than an uncommitted tree. Record both runs with the commit each ran at, judged by the verdict line rather than by the shell exit status. No file outside allowed_paths changes.
constraints: Work only inside the assigned isolated task worktree; never push.
Never use git reset, git checkout --, git stash or git commit --amend.

Do not claim a compatibility check the code does not perform. Every reported verdict must be produced by the code the evidence names, and unknown must be reported as unknown wherever an input is absent.
Do not hand work to a Provider the owner has not authorized, and do not hand work to one whose slot needs an owner's action. Both refusals are acceptance, not preference.
Do not lose the Increment, Artifact or Evidence across a handoff. The existing content digest is the only computation permitted for that claim; do not write a second copy of it.

Do not change any breaker, pool or usage-window behaviour. internal/provider/breaker.go, pool.go and usagewindow.go and their tests are read-only, the d12 opening table is not edited, no FailureClass is added, and no CircuitState, SlotState or WindowState member is added or removed. If the design appears to require one, stop and escalate.
Do not synthesize a FailureClass for a usage-window exhaustion. Exhausting our own attempt ceiling is not a Provider fault and must not be recorded as one.
Do not round unknown to compatible, and do not round unknown to incompatible or exhausted. Unknown is a first-class value on both sides.

Do not widen ProviderObservationInput or any other request DTO whose field list an existing test pins. If a fact cannot reach the control plane without widening one, report it as unknown and name the owner.
Do not change RequestFromHandoff's signature or any of its existing verdicts, and do not edit its existing test cases. The new gate is a single-producer plus an AST single-caller guard.
Do not edit internal/runner/**. It is inside the file set the representative Provider's live exercise compiles, and touching it would force a live re-observation onto this task.
Do not add a UnitOfWork port and do not edit either store adapter. If a stored fact is missing, stop and escalate.

Do not touch ci/components.json, Makefile, go.mod, go.sum or devbox.*. This design creates no new import edge, so a red manifest or dependency-coverage check in make check means the design was departed from: stop and escalate to the tech_lead.

internal/application must import neither internal/provider nor internal/runner. The shared table is re-declared by value and pinned by a test, following the precedent already set twice in this repository.

Do not write a module-path string literal into any source or test file: internal/ci's manifest check reads such a literal as an undeclared edge and turns make check red. Build any needed path by concatenating a prefix with a suffix.
Do not edit contracts/release-contract/** and do not weaken, narrow or reword any clause of cap-provider-operation. Where a clause is not fully satisfied, say which part and who owns it.
Do not edit contracts/schemas/**. Only contracts/openapi/openapi-v1.yaml changes, and only by adding declared fields inside the existing additionalProperties:false schemas.
Do not edit .agents/v2/task-state/**, any .agents/v2/packets/** file, or .agents/v2/provider-preflight/**.

Do not start a Provider CLI and do not make any Provider invocation. --help and --version are the only permitted Provider CLI reads. No fixture may be replaced by captured bytes: the manifest's shape_source declarations stay true.
Both owner console files are effectively single-line minified documents: append a self-contained block introduced by a comment naming V2-074 at the end of each, and change no existing byte.

Determinism is acceptance, not preference: no fixed sleep, no wall-clock timer, no goroutine in any new test. Every instant comes from an injected clock, every table test enumerates its cross product rather than sampling it, and a measured duration is logged as an observation, never asserted as a threshold.
A skipped test is never counted as a pass (gate rule G7). Record every skip with status skipped and its reason, and record the execution environment identifier for every run.

Never write a verification as passed that was not actually executed, and never write that a real Provider was exercised. Contract-fixture evidence satisfies no real-environment condition at any grade; if an acceptance item cannot be satisfied, stop and escalate to the tech_lead rather than fabricating or weakening it.

Retain no prompt and no raw Provider response, and no credential value in any form, in any file, log line or evidence record. The approving person's address in the standing authorization record is never read into any package, response or log line.
Run devbox run --pure -- gitleaks dir .agents --config .gitleaks.toml before every commit that touches .agents/**; never use gitleaks dir . for that scan.
Every pre-existing test must keep passing under its existing name with its existing assertions unchanged. Report before and after top-level test counts per touched package.

Every line number and test count in this Work Order was read at commit 2d1a514 and is expected to be stale. Re-measure each one with go test -list and grep, use the measured value, and report every disagreement.
